title: Identification of key genes related to lymphangiogenesis in venous thromboembolism through transcriptomics and verification by RT-qPCR.
authors: Lin, Yusheng; Wu, Jiahan; Wang, Pucheng; Lin, Xiaodong; Yang, Hongwei
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组和RT-qPCR鉴定静脉血栓栓塞中淋巴管生成相关关键基因，虽涉及TF网络但无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), a life-threatening cardiovascular disorder, involves complex interactions between thrombosis and immune dysregulation. Lymphangiogenesis-related genes (LRGs) may directly induce thrombosis by regulating endothelial function, the coagulation cascade, or inflammatory signaling pathways. This research was intended to uncover LRG-associated key genes and elucidate their molecular mechanisms in VTE. METHODS: Transcriptomic datasets from public databases were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between VTE and control samples. Subsequently, candidate genes were screened by overlapping the DEGs with LRGs obtained from the literature. Functional analysis was then performed on candidate genes. Machine learning algorithms and expression validation were employed to refine key genes. Moreover, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration, and regulatory and disease-gene-drug network analyses were performed. Finally, key genes' expression levels were validated via real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). RESULTS: To sum up, 810 DEGs were identified, of which 30 DEGs were selected as candidate genes. Machine learning and expression validation prioritized MYC and NTAN1 as key genes. Functional analysis revealed their enrichment in spliceosome, oxidative phosphorylation, and immune-related pathways. MYC and NTAN1 correlated with regulatory T cells and M2 macrophages. Furthermore, the microRNA (miRNA)-mRNA-transcription factor (TF) network identified MYC as a hub regulated by hsa-miR-449c-5p and JUN. Disease-gene-drug network highlighted cisplatin and olaparib as potential MYC-targeted therapy. RT-qPCR confirmed MYC downregulation and NTAN1 upregulation in VTE (p < 0.05), consistent with the bioinformatics results. CONCLUSION: This study identified MYC and NTAN1 as pivotal regulators of VTE, bridging thrombotic progression with immune-metabolic dysregulation. The findings provided novel insights into key genes and immunomodulatory therapies for VTE.
abstract_zh: 背景：静脉血栓栓塞症（VTE）是一种危及生命的心血管疾病，涉及血栓形成与免疫失调之间的复杂相互作用。淋巴管生成相关基因（LRGs）可能通过调节内皮功能、凝血级联反应或炎症信号通路直接诱导血栓形成。本研究旨在揭示LRG相关的关键基因，并阐明其在VTE中的分子机制。方法：分析公共数据库中的转录组数据集，以识别VTE与对照样本之间的差异表达基因（DEGs）。随后，通过将DEGs与文献中获得的LRGs重叠来筛选候选基因，并对候选基因进行功能分析。采用机器学习算法和表达验证来精炼关键基因。此外，进行了基因集富集分析（GSEA）、免疫浸润分析以及调控网络和疾病-基因-药物网络分析。最后，通过实时定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR）验证关键基因的表达水平。结果：共识别出810个DEGs，其中30个DEGs被选为候选基因。机器学习和表达验证将MYC和NTAN1确定为主要关键基因。功能分析显示它们富集于剪接体、氧化磷酸化和免疫相关通路。MYC和NTAN1与调节性T细胞和M2巨噬细胞相关。此外，microRNA（miRNA）-mRNA-转录因子（TF）网络将MYC识别为由hsa-miR-449c-5p和JUN调控的核心节点。疾病-基因-药物网络强调顺铂和奥拉帕利为潜在的MYC靶向治疗药物。RT-qPCR证实VTE中MYC下调及NTAN1上调（p < 0.05），与生物信息学结果一致。结论：本研究将MYC和NTAN1确定为VTE的关键调控因子，连接血栓进展与免疫代谢失调。这些发现为VTE的关键基因和免疫调节治疗提供了新见解。
